passages.p1: Read the passage and mark the letter A, B, C or D on your answer sheet to indicate the best answer to each of the following questions from 1 to 8. Microplastics are now widely detected within the human body, yet their biological effects remain only partially understood. Some particles appear to become trapped in the mucus lining the airways and may be cleared before penetrating underlying tissues. Others, however, are capable of travelling further into the body. Evidence from tissue-based studies suggests that the lungs may serve as a major site of accumulation, highlighting inhalation as a significant route of exposure. Particle size is likely to play a decisive role in determining biological impact. Microplastics measuring less than 20 micrometres have been associated with inflammatory responses, while those under five micrometres may cross cellular boundaries and accumulate in multiple organs. Because such particles are not effectively filtered by the nasal passages, they can reach deep lung regions and become lodged there. Experimental findings in animals indicate that inhaled microplastics can disperse rapidly throughout the body and trigger inflammation across several organ systems. Shape, too, appears to influence toxicity. Fibre-like microplastics are considered particularly concerning, as their elongated structure may facilitate deeper penetration into lung tissue and prolong their persistence within the body. Once beyond the lungs, these fibres may enter the bloodstream and lymphatic system, where they have the potential to interfere with cellular processes. Similar concerns have long been associated with other microscopic fibres, although whether microplastics exhibit comparable toxicity remains uncertain. Beyond their potential to interfere with tissues, there's also the concern that microplastics often come with company. They are home to a broad range of bacteria, and may carry other contaminants too. It's been suggested that microplastics might act to amplify the toxicity of other pollutants in the environment. Taken together, these uncertainties point to a field of research that is still in its early stages, with many mechanisms yet to be fully understood. (Adapted from https://www.bbc.co.uk/future)

Held on the full moon each month, the Hoi An Lantern Festival has evolved into one of Viet Nam’s most distinctive cultural spectacles. In recent years, the event has drawn an unprecedented (9) ____________ of international visitors eager to immerse themselves in its atmospheric charm. Local performers deliver highly (10) ____________ displays, seamlessly blending traditional art forms with contemporary elements. The streets, (11) ____________ by hundreds of intricately crafted lanterns, are transformed into a luminous riverside tableau. The festival is widely regarded as a (12) ____________ highlight for those seeking authentic cultural experiences. Visitors, (13) ____________ are keen to engage more deeply with local traditions, often release lanterns onto the river as a symbolic gesture of hope. Beyond its visual appeal, the event also serves as a platform for smaller businesses and artisans to (14) ____________ a distinctive niche in the market and reach a wider audience. (Adapted from Vietnam News)

passages.p4: Read the following passage and mark the letter A, B, C or D on your answer sheet to indicate the correct answer to each of the questions from 20 to 29. The contemporary site design landscape is navigating a precarious intersection of mounting technological demands and workforce instability. Engineering firms, often tethered to the constraints of outdated 2D CAD workflows, are facing significant operational challenges. These traditional processes—reliant on manual labor and suboptimal data sharing—create inefficiencies, resulting in attenuated productivity and a heightened susceptibility to costly errors. [I] An aging workforce and a shortage of skilled professionals have created a formidable expertise gap. The current over-reliance on engineers for both conceptual design and routine drafting create critical bottlenecks, which are exacerbated by the logistical complexities of collaborating across different global time zones. [II] Concurrently, the regulatory environment has become more labyrinthine, imposing stringent compliance standards that demand meticulous attention. This, combined with the industry’s shift toward integrated digital deliverables, forces organizations to undertake complex technological transformations. [III] In this high-pressure atmosphere, defined by tight deadlines and frequent client-driven revisions, the traditional, fragmented approach to project management is no longer sufficient. To succeed in this competitive milieu, forward-thinking firms are adopting solutions like OpenSite+. By prioritizing modern technology, these organizations not only improve their operations but also cultivate a compelling value proposition for tech-savvy, next-generation talent who seek to utilize the latest tools. OpenSite+ represents a paradigmatic shift in civil site engineering, designed to catalyze efficiency through intelligent automation. Central to its design is the AI Drawing Production feature, which addresses the pervasive challenge of tedious, repetitive documentation. [IV] By automatically handling tasks like annotation, labeling, and sheet layout, this feature removes the heavy manual burden traditionally placed on engineers. Consequently, the software facilitates a remarkable acceleration in project delivery, enabling firms to produce construction drawings up to ten times faster than conventional methods. By offloading these routine tasks to AI, OpenSite+ allows engineering professionals to transcend mechanical drafting, refocusing their energy on the analytical and creative problem-solving essential for modern site development. Ultimately, this integration transforms the workflow into a cohesive, data-driven process that supports superior design outcomes. (Adapted from https://blog.bentley.com)
passages.p5: Read the following leaflet and mark the letter A, B, C or D on your answer sheet to indicate the correct word or phrase that best fits each of the numbered blanks from 30 to 35. GREEN ROOFS – AN URBAN TRANSFORMATION Architects have begun to promote green roofs as a viable solution (30) ____________ rising temperatures and energy demands. These installations involve covering rooftops with vegetation, thereby converting underutilized areas into multifunctional spaces. One of the key advantages lies in the creation of (31) ____________ rooftop gardens that can significantly improve urban living conditions. However, the success of such projects often hinges on the amount of rainfall the system is capable of absorbing during periods of intense precipitation. Despite financial constraints, many municipal authorities remain willing (32) ____________ in green infrastructure (33) ____________ its long-term environmental and economic benefits. Furthermore, while some buildings have already adopted this innovation, (34) ____________ continue to exhibit reluctance, often due to structural limitations or maintenance concerns. In addition to moderating urban temperatures, green roofs help to counteract the deleterious effects of air pollution by filtering particulate matter. They also contribute to (35) ____________ biodiversity, as they provide habitats for various species within otherwise inhospitable urban landscapes.
passages.p6: Read the following passage and mark the letter A, B, C or D on your answer sheet to indicate the option that best fits each of the numbered blanks from 36 to 40. Each year, approximately $140 billion is spent globally on conservation, (36) ____________. Yet, for all that money, the public messaging around saving animal species and habitats is almost entirely dire. Although biodiversity loss is real and serious, the data do not support alarmist claims of global, catastrophic wildlife collapse and imminent ecological tipping points. (37) ____________. In response to the largest meeting of conservation scientists in Cali, Colombia, in late 2024, under the auspices of the United Nations’ Convention on Biological Diversity, we reviewed scientists’ understanding of global efforts to stem biodiversity loss. Our work, (38) ____________, recognizes that, while there are gaps in our knowledge of biodiversity loss, conservation has prevented many extinctions and allowed some once-declining species to flourish. (39) ____________, and doing so in sensibly chosen and important locations. There are good news stories to tell: In critically surveying progress over the last 25 years, we see that conservation efforts have prevented extinctions, (40) ____________, and protected ever-greater areas of the planet, both on land and in the ocean. (Adapted from https://foreignpolicy.com)
